title: Ebb-Flow deployment orchestrator: adaptive canary policy with slope-aware deceleration
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Design and implement the 'Ebb-Flow' deployment orchestrator: a policy engine that manages canary rollouts, A/B experiments and shadow probes with slope-aware deceleration, cost-aware throttling, and automatic rollback. This ticket covers the configuration schema, runtime evaluation loop, guardrails, and operator UX for progressive traffic splits and step schedules across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
design_notes:
Core ideas:
- Traffic profile as a first-class object: represent per-cohort traffic curves (initial fraction, max fraction, step cadence, min dwell time, deceleration factor).
- Slope-aware deceleration: compute short-term metric slope (ex. p95 latency slope, failure-rate slope, quality-regression slope) and apply a multiplicative deceleration factor to upcoming step sizes when slopes exceed thresholds.
- Grace windows & forgiveness: allow transient spikes to be discounted using short bloom windows (configurable) and require persistent signals across N windows to trigger rollback.
- Weighted shadow probing: run a percentage of production requests in shadow to new variants; use result weighting to seed canary scoring before traffic switch.
- Safety escrow: reserve a small percentage of traffic (eg 1%) as instant-fallback routing to previous stable variant to enable near-instant mitigation on critical faults.
- Cost-aware throttling: provide budget caps per rollout that throttle expansion based on estimated token cost burn to avoid runaway spend during large A/B experiments.
- DSL shape: keep config YAML/JSON-friendly: 'stages' array with 'fraction', 'min_dwell', 'max_dwell', 'conditions' and optional 'decay_policy' referencing telemetry signals.
- Observability: emit step decisions, deceleration triggers, shadow mismatch rates, and rollback rationale as discrete events for Console and audit logs.
- Compatible with existing rollout primitives but introduces slope-based dynamic step adjustments and shadow seeding.
acceptance_criteria: Provide a rollout configuration schema that supports staged fractions, min_dwell, max_dwell, conditional deceleration, shadow probing, and cost caps.
Runtime evaluates and applies deceleration when configured signal slopes exceed thresholds, reducing next step fraction by configured multiplier.
Automatic rollback triggers on sustained critical-signal violation (configurable windows) and routes traffic immediately to safety escrow variant.
Console shows per-rollout timeline with step annotations, deceleration events, shadow probe scores, and rollback reasoning.
Unit and integration tests cover telemetry edge cases (transient spikes vs sustained regressions) and cost-throttling behavior.
Performance: decision loop latency < 100ms and scales to 10k concurrent rollouts in Dedicated clusters (empirical target).
rollout_configuration_schema: Example fields: name, base_variant, candidate_variant, stages:[{fraction, min_dwell, max_dwell, allow_manual_advance:false, decay_policy:{signal, slope_threshold, multiplier}}], shadow:{enabled, fraction}, safety_escrow_fraction, cost_cap_per_hour, rollback_policies:[{signal, window_seconds, threshold, severity}], observability_tags:[...]. Schema must be JSON-schema compatible and validated at create-time.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Schema + lightweight evaluator service (k8s) that accepts rollout config and current telemetry, returns next action (advance, hold, decelerate, rollback).
Phase 2: Integrate evaluator into routing plane to enforce step fractions and safety escrow for fast fallback.
Phase 3: Shadow probing integration: extend request router to duplicate requests for variants with weight, collect mismatch metrics and feed to evaluator.
Phase 4: Console UI hooks and audit log events, add rollout timeline visualization and manual override controls.
Phase 5: Load testing and scale tuning (target 10k concurrent rollouts for Dedicated).
Phase 6: Rollout to staging, then pilot with two internal teams, iterate on deceleration thresholds and grace windows.
testing_plan: Simulated traffic harness that can inject controlled latency and error slopes to validate slope-aware deceleration and rollback windows.
Chaos tests: kill candidate variant nodes while running shadow probes to ensure safety escrow fallback works under network partitions.
Cost-simulation: inject token-cost multipliers to ensure cost_cap_per_hour throttles growth as expected.
A/B correctness: statistical checks for sample bias when running weighted shadow probing and seeding canary scoring.
End-to-end smoke with Console: create a rollout, run through auto-advance, induce deceleration and ensure events are visualized and logged.
